  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) for each of the five response variables separately, with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "Test the null hypothesis that the mean performance metric is equal across all five stimulation paradigms for each variable.",
    "Check for homogeneity of variances (Levene's test) and normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk test) for each variable before proceeding to post-hoc tests.",
    "If assumptions are met, proceed to post-hoc pairwise comparisons; if variances are unequal, use Welch's ANOVA followed by Games-Howell post-hoc tests."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Conduct pairwise t-tests between all 10 unique pairs of stimulation paradigms for each response variable.",
    "Calculate the mean difference and 95% confidence intervals for each pair.",
    "Report p-values adjusted for multiple comparisons to determine statistical significance between specific paradigms.",
    "Identify which specific paradigms differ significantly from the Sham control and from each other."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Apply the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (Benjamini-Hochberg procedure) to the p-values from all post-hoc pairwise comparisons to control the expected proportion of false positives while maintaining higher statistical power than the Bonferroni correction.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Since the response variables are continuous (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) but Success is binary (0/1), a single linear model is inappropriate for Success. The recommended approach is a multivariate framework: use One-Way ANOVA (or Linear Mixed Models with 'Mouse' as a random effect to account for repeated measures) for the continuous variables, and One-Way ANOVA on the log-odds (Logistic Regression) for Success. Alternatively, a Multinomial Logistic Regression could be used if Success were treated as a categorical outcome, but given the binary nature, separate models per variable are statistically rigorous.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify that data points are independent or account for the 'Mouse' factor as a random effect in a Mixed Model.",
    "Normality of residuals: Check Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for each response variable within each paradigm group.",
    "Homogeneity of variances: Perform Levene's test or Bartlett's test across the five paradigm groups for each response variable.",
    "Linearity: Not applicable for ANOVA, but relevant if extending to regression; verify linear relationships if modeling continuous predictors.",
    "Binary distribution check: Confirm 'Success' follows a binomial distribution (0 or 1) and does not contain outliers or missing values."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm is hypothesized to show superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to 'Sham' and single-modality paradigms.",
    "The 'ICMS Only' and 'Dim Visual Only' paradigms may show intermediate performance, potentially differing significantly from 'Sham' but not from 'Combined'.",
    "The 'Bright Visual Only' paradigm may perform similarly to 'Sham' or slightly better, depending on the specific task constraints.",
    "Significant main effects of 'Stim Paradigm' are expected for all five response variables given the large sample size (n=76655) and distinct theoretical mechanisms of the paradigms.",
    "Interaction effects are not expected as the design is a one-way ANOVA, but the magnitude of effect sizes may vary across response variables."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset includes 8 different mouse strains; without explicitly modeling 'Mouse' as a random effect, individual strain variability may inflate Type I error rates or mask true effects.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption required for standard ANOVA; a transformation or non-parametric test (Kruskal-Wallis) or logistic regression is strictly required for this variable.",
    "Path Efficiency has a wide range (0.0009 to 29.8), which may indicate skewness or outliers that could violate ANOVA assumptions.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm has the largest sample size (48846), which may lead to statistically significant but practically negligible differences compared to smaller groups.",
    "Causality cannot be definitively established without controlling for all potential confounding variables beyond the stimulation paradigm."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM) for the continuous variables and Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMM) with a binomial link for Success, including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for within-subject correlation and repeated measures across paradigms."
}
